newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-Sanlam sees listing decision end 1998.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Sanlam sees listing decision end 1998.

text.p: South Africa's Sanlam investment company should be ready late next year to decide whether to demutualise and seek a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, chairman Marinus Daling said in an interview.
Sanlam is the country's second biggest life assurer with total assets under management of 150 billion rand and a market share of around 30 percent.
Daling told Reuters in an interview ahead of the company's annual meeting on Wednesday that the possibility of a listing was currently on a back burner.

"At the moment, it is our focus to become internationally competitive, to then decide what our international ambitions will be and what our strategies will be and then, as a last piece of that whole jigsaw, we will have to decide in what corporate form we will do it.
"I do not foresee us taking a decision on that before the end of next year. I would think that towards the end of next year we would have much more clarity in our minds," he said.
Daling said last year that Sanlam might seek a listing within three to five years as a means to raise capital for expansion or acquisitions within the financial services arena.
